items.summary: On Tuesday, November 10 in Sydney, Australia announced mandatory reporting requirements for artificial intelligence companies covering misaligned behaviour and cyber incidents, following an OpenAI agent breach of a government website in June. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the government accepted all recommendations from a rapid review into the incident.
items.title: Australia Mandates AI Incident Reporting After OpenAI Government Breach

items.summary: A profile examines why Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is regarded as indispensable to the AI industry, drawing crowds in Taipei and Seoul and reportedly persuading billionaires Larry Ellison and Elon Musk to fund his chips. Analysts note that Nvidia has turned its cash into a war chest backing cloud providers and labs, which some see as a risk after Huang confirmed an affair with a Chinese businesswoman accused of passing information to Beijing. Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon called the news negative for stewardship debates. Dan Ives said Jensen is not replaceable. The article notes Nvidia has no disclosed succession plan and that over 60 executives report directly to him, though he holds only about a 3.6% stake without special voting shares.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Seen as Indispensable but Risky for AI Industry

items.summary: Jensen Huang, Nvidia's chief executive and a central figure in the AI industry, has become the subject of scrutiny after admitting an affair with Alice Huang, whom US intelligence concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset. Nvidia announced it would investigate whether company policies were violated; federal authorities may also look into possible legal violations or influence over chip-export policy. Shares fell more than 4 percent on Monday. Analysts warn that no comparable executive exists and that the scandal could accelerate tighter controls on exports to China.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Faces Investigation Over Alleged Affair With Chinese Intelligence Asset

items.summary: On 9th November 2026, Anthropic released Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, added to the llm-anthropic tool so prompts can run through claude-fable-5.2. The author tested pelicans at five reasoning levels (low, medium, high, xhigh, max); the best came from xhigh. Max failed entirely, running out of tokens after 128,000 thinking about them — a bug also seen with Opus 5.5 and new to the Fable series, since earlier versions returned results fine.
items.title: Anthropic Ships Fable and Mythos Model Updates

items.summary: Despite a major Nasdaq sell-off and revelations about an AI CEO's affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Anthropic is proceeding with its initial public offering. According to The Wall Street Journal, the company plans to set a valuation range this week and begin trading next Thursday or Friday.
items.title: Anthropic Moves Forward With IPO Plans Despite Market Uncertainty

items.summary: President Donald Trump said Monday that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang should not worry about an FBI investigation into his affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese government agent, telling reporters at the White House he believed Huang would be in good shape. The disclosure follows reports from The New York Times that intelligence officials found the woman gathering information for Beijing and that Huang had admitted intimacy with a business executive without naming her. Nvidia said it was conducting an independent investigation into claims Huang was targeted by foreign intelligence, while China denied any spying effort, calling the allegation unsubstantiated. Nvidia shares fell roughly 5% in pre-market trading.
items.title: Trump Defends Nvidia Chief Amid Spy Probe

items.summary: Beijing dismissed allegations that it spied on Nvidia's CEO as 'smears against China,' warning the controversy could strain bilateral ties ahead of next week's Trump-Xi meeting. A former state media editor framed the dispute as a Democratic Party effort to target Jensen Huang and, by extension, President Trump, while commentators praised access to what one analyst called the world's most important company.
items.title: China Rejects Espionage Allegations Against Jensen Huang Ahead of Trump-Xi Meeting

items.summary: Nvidia shares fell 4.4% in premarket trading on Monday, according to Axios, following Friday's Nasdaq closing price of $186.64. The move represented a potential loss of around $199 billion in market value. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair with Alice Huang and accepted responsibility for his actions. An independent board committee is investigating reports that he was targeted by foreign intelligence, though the allegations have not been established. China's Foreign Ministry rejected the claims as smears on Monday. Analysts say uncertainty around leadership could affect investors ahead of Nvidia earnings on November 17 and a congressional briefing on November 18; AMD shares may benefit while Asian suppliers rebounded despite the sell-off.
items.title: Nvidia Shares Fall as Board Investigates Jensen Huang

items.summary: The Indian Rupee strengthened from ₹95.26 on October 29 to around ₹93.85 on November 9, marking a notable recovery against the US Dollar after months of Reserve Bank of India intervention. The turnaround follows easing tensions with Iran, falling crude oil prices and renewed foreign institutional investor inflows into Indian stock markets.
items.title: Indian Rupee Stages Strong Comeback Against Dollar After Months of RBI Intervention

items.summary: Ahead of the Abu Dhabi trilateral peace dialogue, Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy spoke with PM Narendra Modi on Monday to press India toward a ceasefire. Zelensky urged India to take concrete steps and said food security could be key, citing blocked Black Sea grain routes. Modi called it their first conversation since June's G7 summit and described the talk as productive.
items.title: Zelenskyy Urges Modi for Ceasefire Help Before Peace Talks

items.summary: Cevenini, Costello and Fezzi present the first causal estimate of how ocean temperature affects fishing revenue. Using about 2.5 million observations across all European vessels from 2013 to 2022, they find that deviations from species’ thermal preferences reduce revenue, with heat exposure causing the largest losses. Projections suggest widespread declines by 2100, reaching €560 million annually in the warmest scenario, though impacts vary widely across regions.
items.title: Study Estimates Climate Change Losses in European Fisheries Revenue

items.summary: Amy Finkelstein, Matthew J. Notowidigdo, and Charlie Rafkin analyze the 1979 reform that made food stamps free. The change raised enrollment by 1.85 percentage points (standard error = 0.15), or about 25%, with recipients valuing them at 59 cents per dollar. Infant health did not improve, though social welfare rose from better targeting.
items.title: Study Finds Free Food Stamps Raised Enrollment but Not Infant Health

items.summary: A Supreme Court bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Manmohan ordered the immediate release of an accused in an abetment-of-suicide case after he remained detained for one and a half months because lawyers refused to represent him before the trial court in Baghpat, Uttar Pradesh. The bench termed the situation very unusual and directed release on a personal bond of Rs 10,000.
items.title: Supreme Court Orders Release After Lawyers' Boycott Keeps Accused Detained

items.summary: Qantas is preparing to cut about 850 Australian jobs and move some work offshore under an AI-driven overhaul, part of a wave of corporate layoffs in Australia. The airline signed a multi-year deal with Accenture to modernise its systems while investing more in technology and AI. Some services will shift to Accenture’s India-based team. Chief executive Vanessa Hudson said staff would be consulted before final decisions, with changes taking effect by mid-next year.
items.title: Qantas Plans Major Job Cuts and Offshore Outsourcing Amid AI Overhaul

items.summary: In a Shelby County courthouse, Alabama Power attorney Jim Byram told Judge Jonathan Spann that landowner Fenn Church repeatedly said he wanted to be arrested or run over by a bulldozer. The two sides dispute whether Alabama Power may build a transmission line across Church’s rural property near Columbiana, which he says could support data center infrastructure. A judge had issued a preliminary injunction in Church’s favor last month after finding the company failed state condemnation procedures; that order was stayed by the Alabama Supreme Court on Oct. 21 without written reasoning, and crews cleared land to his line by Nov. 3. At Monday’s hearing, lawyers argued over whether Alabama Power may proceed while the underlying case remains litigated in the Supreme Court.
items.title: Alabama Power Attorney Dismisses Landowner’s Claims in Transmission Line Fight

items.summary: A woman raped by Jeffrey Epstein says the president of her model agency, Jeff Fuller, put her in danger by sending her to photoshoots at his Florida beach house while he was jailed. Roza tells the BBC World Service that the agency failed its duty to protect her and should be held accountable. She shows an expense statement suggesting Fuller booked her flight home from Palm Beach after a second shoot there. Fuller has not responded, having previously claimed ignorance of her whereabouts. The article draws on Epstein-related documents released by the US Department of Justice showing 10 MC2 models met or communicated with Epstein after his conviction and that he gave $1m (£742,000) to MC2 in 2005. New York senator Zellnor Myrie is challenging a statement that no evidence warrants further investigation against uncharged third parties and has proposed new sex trafficking legislation.
items.title: Epstein Abuse Survivor Accuses Model Agency President of Endangering Her

items.summary: US officials said Moscow and Kyiv are privately showing 'a little bit of flexibility' over who would control Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar scenario, ahead of the first trilateral talks since February. Jared Kushner framed the discussions around Russia's and Ukraine's 'postwar security concerns,' while an unnamed US official noted that resolving Donetsk depends on agreeing a new security architecture. Moscow has demanded Ukraine give up remaining parts of Donetsk; Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line. European leaders, largely excluded so far, pressed for inclusion, with von der Leyen urging Nato and EU involvement. Ukrainian MP Oleksandr Merezhko warned Trump seeks 'a quick deal at the expense of Ukraine,' which he said would be rejected by Kyiv.
items.title: Ukraine peace talks resume with cautious flexibility

items.summary: The Multi-Commodity Exchange of India (MCX) will suspend trading during the morning session from 9 am to 5 pm on Tuesday, resuming in the evening session until 11:30 pm. The National Commodity & Derivatives Exchange Limited (NCDEX) remains closed all day for Diwali-Balipratipada. Of the 16 stock market holidays scheduled for 2026, 13 have already been observed, with the next closure on November 24 and December 25 remaining.
items.title: Indian Exchanges Mark Diwali-Balipratipada Trading Holiday in 2026

items.summary: Paris-based French officials accused Iran's Revolutionary Guard on Monday of responsibility for cyberattacks that disabled commercial refrigerators and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across France in early October. They said consequences would follow for Tehran, framing the strikes as among the most disruptive digital incidents of an ongoing conflict marked by scattered alleged attacks.
items.title: French Officials Blame Iran's Revolutionary Guard for Refrigerator Hacks and Vow Retaliation

items.summary: A headteacher said families will struggle after school dinner prices rise for the second time in a year, with pre-primary meals up 30p and post-primary pupils facing a 15% increase. The move follows an earlier January increase of just under 20% by the Education Authority (EA). Áine Leslie of Malone Integrated College said the cumulative effect would be immense amid the cost of living crisis. Other educators called the rise excessive or unreasonable, warning it could harm children's health and learning. The EA cited insufficient funding and plans to save £20m on top of £30m already saved this year.
items.title: Headteachers Warn Families Struggle as School Dinner Prices Rise Again

items.summary: Anthropic is aiming to raise as much as $69.3 billion, potentially among the largest initial public offerings on record, per a copy of a filing seen by Reuters on Monday. The figure comes from an unpublished document rather than a confirmed prospectus, so it reflects intent reported through a source that has not independently verified the offering.
items.title: Anthropic Targets Up To $69.3 Billion in Record IPO

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India extended the supersession of the Board of Directors of Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank, Mumbai, by one year. The bank was first superseded in November 2023 over poor governance standards. On review, the RBI said it is satisfied that extending the period serves public interest beyond business close on November 23, 2026. Administrator Satya Prakash Pathak will continue, assisted by advisors Venkatesh Hegde, Devendra Kumar and Suhas Gokhale.
items.title: RBI Extends Supersession of Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Board for Another Year

items.summary: The author built Beep Locator, software that triangulates the source of an intermittent beep in their box room using several devices acting as listeners. After running it for some time without good results, they added Rough mode and clapping tests; beeps appear on the map as X marks plus log entries, which can be replayed to confirm them before locking onto a location within about 40cm—revealing an old carbon monoxide detector needing batteries. The system runs a Python web server with WebSockets feeding browser microphones that record audio and run beep detection; it also lets Claude Code receive new code over the connection, effectively giving the coding agent ears to perceive sound for the first time.
items.title: A developer gives Claude Code ears to locate a beep

items.summary: Nvidia’s stock fell more than 4% on Monday, the first trading day after its board announced an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang over his relationship with Alice Huang. Securities lawyers quickly moved; at least four firms opened investigations into whether Nvidia misled investors. By Monday afternoon, Rosen Law Firm filed a class-action complaint in the Northern District of California on behalf of investor Mark Kistenmacher, covering purchases between Oct. 9, 2025 and Nov. 8, 2026. Stanford law professor Robert Bartlett expects more filings and predicts a “classic fraud on the market” claim tied to Monday’s $7.97-per-share drop. The suit rests on statements about Huang’s ties to Megaspeed that it calls false; damages are unspecified but could be large, though such cases usually settle without personal consequences for executives.
items.title: Nvidia Faces Securities Lawsuits After Stock Slide

items.summary: Anthropic unveiled two new AI models, Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, on Monday as it prepares for a planned initial public offering. The company said the models produce outputs up to 30 per cent faster than their Claude 5.1 predecessors. They will be priced lower at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. Fable 5.2 targets coding, reasoning and AI agent tasks; Mythos 5.2 is limited to approved cybersecurity and life-sciences research organisations. The release follows Claude Haiku 5.5's October rollout amid intensifying competition from OpenAI, Alphabet's Google and Meta Platforms.
items.title: Anthropic Launches Faster, Cheaper Claude Models Ahead of IPO

items.summary: A scandal involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who admitted an affair with a woman suspected of spying for Chinese intelligence services, has drawn criticism over the company's governance and succession planning. Analysts note its board lacks experienced directors and that Huang oversees more than 50 direct reports without a clear successor. The SEC's former chair said it appears Huang misled the public, while Nvidia's shares fell 5%, reducing market value by $200 billion. Nvidia maintains confidence in Huang and says no national security or company secrets were compromised.
items.title: Nvidia's board faces scrutiny amid Jensen Huang spy allegations

items.summary: Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic says at least six memecoin tokens were created on the NEAR blockchain within days of the US$6.3 billion Binance heist to launder about US$430,000 of stolen crypto. The tokens traded briefly before being abandoned and bore cartoon-style logos. Tom Robinson, Elliptic’s founder, said such short-lived meme coins attract little attention.
items.title: Binance Hackers Laundered Stolen Crypto via Memecoins, Elliptic Says

items.summary: A new ASEAN Green Jobs Report, released Oct 27 during the ALSN launch in Singapore and based mostly on LinkedIn data, found fewer than 1% of regional workers are in green jobs. Singapore had the lowest share; construction hires were up to 25.2%, utilities over 30%. Authors noted renewable energy could create potentially over 5.5 million jobs by 2050, though such roles remain poorly identified and data was skewed toward higher-skilled work.
items.title: ASEAN Green Jobs Report Finds Under 1% of Workers in Green Roles

items.summary: An investigation into Nvidia is being overseen by a committee of independent directors, reportedly assisted by outside legal counsel. Nvidia states it has no reason to believe company or national security secrets have been compromised. The developments revive attention on founder Jensen Huang's children, Spencer and Madison. Spencer works in product management at Nvidia, specialising in robotics and simulation, having joined the company in 2022 after co-founding R&D Cocktail Lab in Taiwan and completing an MBA at New York University's Stern School of Business.
items.title: Jensen Huang's son builds Nvidia's robot push

items.summary: Jensen Huang, chief executive of Nvidia, has admitted being unfaithful to his wife and apologised to his family amid allegations that he was targeted by a possible Chinese intelligence honey-trap. His board launched an independent investigation into whether the allegations are true. China dismissed the claims as unfounded, while President Donald Trump defended him; Secretary of State Marco Rubio declined to comment.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Admits Infidelity Amid Chinese Espionage Claims

items.summary: Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen reportedly recruited by Beijing to gather intelligence on Jensen Huang, head of Nvidia, is the subject of an accusation detailed in media reports. Public information about her remains limited; she was previously linked to Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based data centre firm that rents computing power for AI training and operations. Reports describe alleged surveillance activities amid US-China competition over advanced AI with military applications. Huang's connection to Jensen Huang has drawn attention through photos from industry events in 2024 and 2025. The New York Times reported the spy plot, while US officials reportedly concluded last year that she was targeting Jensen Huang. Megaspeed faced scrutiny by Singapore authorities, who questioned her in 2025, and Bloomberg News covered a related investigation into alleged chip smuggling to China. AFP could not independently verify details of an online profile listing her past roles at HSBC and Chinese media outlets CCTV and Hunan TV.
items.title: Chinese Executive Accused of Spying on Nvidia CEO

items.summary: Qantas will outsource roughly 850 local corporate jobs to Accenture, with most positions moving to India and some remaining in Australia. CEO Vanessa Hudson announced the plan via an internal email on Tuesday, saying it is hard news for affected staff. The changes begin mid-2027 and target finance, procurement, people and marketing roles as Qantas modernises its IT systems amid rising technology spending.
items.title: Qantas Outsources Corporate Roles as It Accelerates AI Investment

items.summary: A teenager who pleaded guilty to planning a terrorist attack in Sydney in 2024 told the court he was radicalised online after seeing extremist material on TikTok and used ChatGPT to shape his plans. The New South Wales Supreme Court ordered him into a three-year community corrections order instead of jail, with Justice Stephen Campbell noting his deradicalisation is well advanced. OpenAI, Telegram and YouTube were approached for comment; TikTok declined.
items.title: Sydney Teenager Who Planned Terror Attack Tells Court He Used AI

items.summary: Central Japan Railway officials say the new Nagoya Station for the Chuo Shinkansen line will not finish until at least 2033. JR Central announced this estimate during a briefing for local residents over Sunday and Monday, following delays of up to 3 years in two sections from the original plan because of extra work such as removing underground obstacles. The company had abandoned its target of launching maglev services between Shinagawa Station and Nagoya Station in 2027 but plans to set a new opening date within this year.
items.title: JR Central Pushes Nagoya Maglev Station Completion Past 2033

items.summary: In a metals sector scorecard, JSW Steel clocked record quarterly orders worth ₹1.5 lakh crore while reporting double-digit revenue and profit growth, with like-to-like volume up 13% year-on-year (s39). However, profitability faced pressure from material cost inflation as Ebitda margin fell 130 basis points sequentially to 8.7% (s17,s41). Tata Steel's domestic Ebitda rose 10% on robust 16% volume growth (s40), while JSW Steel's Ebitda margin slipped to 18.6% and Tata Steel UK continued posting an Ebitda loss from lower deliveries (s41,s42). Across the sector, revenue grew 28.7% year-on-year with net profit up 101.3%, though ferrous realisations softened sequentially amid weaker long steel prices (s45). Outlook points to improving domestic steel realisations in the second half of FY27, but higher coking coal prices may weigh on near-term profitability (s44).
items.title: JSW Steel Orders and Margins Under Pressure Amid Inflation

items.summary: More than 500 people invaded the Ituna/Itatá Indigenous Territory, home to the isolated Igarapé Ipiaçava people. Brazil has deployed the National Public Security Force for 180 days to support Funai’s protection work. A Mongabay investigation found a fast-tracked state law helped legitimize and encourage hundreds of invaders, who smashed gates and set up camps; forest-fire alerts rose from zero in August to 23 by Oct. 13.
items.title: Brazil deploys security force after invasion of Indigenous territory in Pará

items.summary: A Finshots story explains how venture-backed startups and large tech firms are changing the traditional defence model, in which governments funded research and owned weapons outright. Historically the US relied on private contractors building state-directed technology; today AI, cloud computing and satellites drive a shift toward companies that keep ownership of their software and infrastructure while militaries rent access, described as an equipment layer versus permission layer distinction. Examples include SpaceX's Starlink terminals used by Ukraine since 2022 and Indian defence-tech funding rising from $135.2 million in 2024 to $282.5 million in 2025 after Operation Sindoor in May 2025. The piece argues governments should retain control over deployment, access and service continuity rather than surrendering critical infrastructure. It offers no picture plan (decision: none).
items.title: Startups and Big Tech Reshape Modern Defence

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department forecast isolated heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu on November 9 and 10, with snowfall likely in parts of Kashmir Valley on November 12 and 13. Separately, the Commission for Air Quality Management recorded Delhi's air quality index at 311 early Tuesday, classifying it as 'very poor.' Private agencies reported higher readings amid questions about monitoring coverage and measurement methods.
items.title: IMD Warns of Heavy Rainfall; Delhi Air Quality Stays Very Poor

items.summary: Petrol and diesel prices stayed flat across Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru and Hyderabad on November 10. The Centre removed excise duty on petrol exports, yet local taxes kept rates unchanged. Brent crude fell $5.75 to settle at $92.57 a barrel after Trump said he is unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran.
items.title: Indian fuel prices hold steady as crude falls on Iran de-escalation hopes

items.summary: Wade Derksen, a Carlton Football Club player and father of three, was fined $873 and banned from driving for 12 months after pleading guilty to high-range drink driving at Darwin Local Court. He did not appear in person but pleaded by telephone. Police stopped him on the Arnhem Highway south of Darwin in September following a random breath test that recorded a blood-alcohol reading of 0.174, three times the legal limit.
items.title: Carlton player Derksen suspended for drink driving conviction

items.summary: Todd Russell, a former miner trapped underground for 14 nights when the Beaconsfield Gold Mine collapsed in 2006, has died at age 54 from an undisclosed illness. Fellow survivor Brant Webb paid tribute to him, saying the collapse would always connect them and that they had 'gone through something together all those years ago'. Russell retired as chief of the Beaconsfield Fire Brigade earlier this year after a 31-year career and became a mental health advocate. Tasmanian Premier Jeremy Rockliff, Deputy Premier Guy Barnett, Launceston mayor Matthew Garwood and former West Tamar mayor Barry Easther offered tributes to his resilience and community service.
items.title: Former Beaconsfield survivor Todd Russell dies aged 54

items.summary: A new round of trilateral negotiations between Russia, Ukraine and the United States is scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday in Abu Dhabi, months after earlier US-mediated peace talks in January and February failed. US special envoy Steve Witkoff said discussions would focus on post-war security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian efforts and next steps toward peace. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy named his key topics as security guarantees, an energy ceasefire, unblocking the Black Sea, prisoner exchanges and preparations for a leaders' meeting. Lawmakers and analysts warn of limited progress; Hanna Shelest said Russia may use the talks to stall while continuing attacks.
items.title: Trilateral Russia-Ukraine-US talks set for Abu Dhabi

items.summary: Shehnaz Khanum lived for nearly a decade in Viklang Basti, a slum of about 50 disabled people near Sewa Nagar railway station in Central Delhi. In January 2009, around 22 bulldozers demolished the settlement ahead of the Commonwealth Games; within a year a parking lot served Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium visitors. The Delhi government ran evictions that left nearly two lakh persons homeless, per the Housing and Land Rights Network. Khanum's family relocated to Savda Ghevra in December 2011, but unprepared plots amid farmland forced them back within months. She now lives on a pavement near a Sai Baba temple with other disabled residents, as no dedicated housing schemes exist for persons with disabilities in Delhi.
items.title: Disabled Delhi Residents Return to Pavement After Failed Resettlement

items.summary: A study of more than 21,000 trees at the Wanang Forest Dynamics Plot in northern Papua New Guinea found that tree mortality was significantly higher after the 2015-17 El Niño drought than before or during it. Lead author Hayden Wagia said the post-drought deaths were visible as many trees kept dying once rainfall returned. The effect varied by location: valley trees recovered quickly, while ridge trees showed elevated mortality that stayed high afterward. Researchers say they cannot yet determine what caused the delayed deaths and warn findings may not apply to higher-elevation forests.
items.title: Study Finds Delayed Tree Deaths After El Niño Drought in Papua New Guinea

items.summary:
US President Donald Trump said on Monday that the war with Iran was militarily effectively over, suggesting he was not planning large-scale attacks soon. He described negotiations as showing positive momentum and told reporters they were talking politely. However, Trump warned American forces remained locked and loaded, ready to strike if circumstances changed. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the next move rested with Trump. Meanwhile, Iran rejected reports of talks, demanding an end to the blockade, sanctions relief and compensation. The US State Department issued Level 4 travel advisories for six countries in the region, including Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, Libya, Syria and Yemen, calling them dangerous. AP reported Republicans lost control of Congress amid public dissatisfaction over fuel prices and the conflict's eight-month toll on the global economy.

visual:null},
items.title: Trump Signals War With Iran Is Over But Warns Forces Stay Ready

items.summary: The Odisha Cabinet approved 13 proposals spanning power, education, recruitment and agriculture. Among them is a rule change removing all restrictions on attempts for the state civil services examination until candidates reach their upper age limit. The decisions were taken at a meeting chaired by Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi in Bhubaneswar.
items.title: Odisha Cabinet Approves Unlimited Civil Services Exam Attempts

items.summary: Trucking startup Humble Robotics raised more than $75 million, including a $51 million Series A led by Obvious Ventures with participation from Eclipse and Energy Impact Partners. The round will fund the company’s move from prototype to preproduction of its driverless, cab-less, truck-less battery-electric freight platform intended for dock-to-dock containerized cargo operations. Founder and CEO Eyal Cohen said Humble has spent years proving a truck can drive itself, while noting that making autonomy dependable every day remains harder. The company claims it completed its first prototype in under six months and plans to begin autonomous testing with logistics partners using cameras, lidar, radar, and vision-language-action models. Coverage notes the article was originally published 06MAY26.
items.title: Humble Robotics Raises $75 Million for Truckless Autonomous Trailers

items.summary: The Congress alleges that keeping Parliament's Monsoon Session open for a record 88 days signals an attempt to pass delimitation bills. The session, which began in July and was adjourned sine die on August 13, has not been formally prorogued under Article 85 of the Constitution. Jairam Ramesh accused Union Home Minister Amit Shah of seeking a two-thirds majority for legislation expanding the Lok Sabha to as many as 850 seats and advancing women's reservations using outdated census data. The bill failed on April 17 with 298 votes against the required 352, but realignments have brought the NDA closer to the threshold. Congress maintains that no sitting is confirmed despite the delay.
items.title: Congress Alleges Plot Behind Parliament's Record Session Delay

items.summary: The Duchess of Sussex withdrew from a planned joint speech with her son Harry at the European Parliament in Brussels, citing that she did not feel emotionally strong enough to speak publicly after Thomas Markle Sr.'s arrest on federal child sexual abuse material charges. The report noted she would still attend but not speak.
items.title: Meghan Markle Withdraws From Brussels Speech After Father's Arrest

items.summary: Police said six members of each of two families died in separate overnight fires during early Monday Diwali celebrations, one in Katni and one in Seoni district. In Katni, an earthen lamp reportedly triggered the blaze; police said its cause remains under investigation. The state government directed ₹4 lakh assistance for each family of the deceased.
items.title: Madhya Pradesh official announces aid after two Diwali fires kill 12

items.summary: In her new memoir Belonging, former Congress chief Sonia Gandhi says she has had practically no real contact with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. They now greet each other only formally at semi-official gatherings like the Speaker’s chamber, unlike past cordiality between leaders across party divides. She acknowledges differing ideologies but also some common ground and his rise from an underprivileged background within the RSS. The book arrives Tuesday in stores; author Sunetra Choudhury writes it.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi's Memoir Reveals Little Contact With Modi

items.summary: PlugShare is overhauling its EV charging app with version 8.0, arriving worldwide on November 10 for iPhone. The update adds dark mode that follows the phone's settings, a trip planner showing distances between charging stops, refreshed location tabs, zoomable station photos, and an adapted layout for the iPhone Duo. A rebuilt Apple Watch app lists nearby stations with PlugScore, network details, plug types including NACS, CCS, CHAdeMO, or J1772, and wrist refresh updates. The update rolls out through the App Store.
items.title: PlugShare rolls out dark mode and app refresh for iPhone users

items.summary: Right-wing attacks on Left bookstalls during Kali Puja continued, with a stall outside the CPI(M)'s Bankura district office vandalised by four to five people on November 9. The CPI(M) accused BJP and RSS supporters; BJP denied it. Book sales reportedly rose about 70 per cent compared with Rs 90.12 lakh in 2025, reaching Rs 1.53 crore during Durga Puja. Party leaders said public condemnation strengthened their outreach efforts. The CPI(M) set up 14 stalls in Kolkata this year against eight last year and plans a door-to-door book campaign from November 15. BJP dismissed the plan as insignificant; whether it succeeds remains to be seen.
items.title: CPI(M) Turns Bookstall Vandalism Into Political Opportunity

items.summary: Boeing said on Monday it will cut about 5% of its commercial plane workforce through layoffs and attrition as it slows the ramp-up of jet production to give factories time to stabilize. Boeing commercial chief Stephanie Pope attributed the move to adjusting schedules after US certifications this year for the 737 Max 7 and 10, while CEO Kelly Ortberg said full stability may take into next year at its Kansas operation. Layoff notifications are expected to begin in December.
items.title: Boeing Trims Commercial Workforce Amid Slower Jet Production Ramp

items.summary: Russian diesel tankers have diverted from U.S. destinations, complicating President Trump's October 9 agreement with Vladimir Putin to ease fuel prices by releasing more than 300,000 metric tonnes immediately, then 500,000 tonnes in November and another 1 million tonnes thereafter. The Treasury authorized covered transactions through April 7 next year via License No. 135, but the Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act bans such imports unless Congress certifies specific conditions. Lawmakers warn handlers could face penalties; New Jersey's Governor Sherrill urged ports to turn cargoes away. Kpler analyst Matt Smith attributed uncertainty to buyers' legal concerns. Meanwhile, U.S. diesel prices averaged $6.17 a gallon on November 9, with inventories down 3.6 million barrels. As Alex Kimani for Oilprice.com.
items.title: U.S. Traders Weigh Legal Risk of Russian Diesel Imports

items.summary: An explosion at a steel plant in Izmir province killed 17 people on Monday, November 9, after an overhead crane collapsed into an electric arc furnace during maintenance. İzmir governor Süleyman Elban said the accident damaged a gas line and triggered the blast. AFP reported that around 120 tonnes of molten steel fell onto the furnace, while roughly 200 employees were present at the site.
items.title: Turkey Steel Plant Explosion Kills 17 Workers in Izmir

items.summary: Political rivals Poland's Tusk and Nawrocki attended a memorial for six victims of the 7 November shooting in Kraków, placing candles among those already left there. Footage showed mourners gathered as bullet marks remained visible on nearby café windows. The rare joint appearance comes amid their dispute over reforms to Poland's Constitutional Tribunal, offering unity despite ongoing political differences.
items.title: Polish Rivals Unite at Kraków Shooting Memorial

items.summary: At the opening plenary of UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, climate chief Simon Stiell said a global fossil fuel price crisis is spreading inflation like a cancer. He attributed surging petrol prices worldwide to Donald Trump's war with Iran and disruption of the Strait of Hormuz oil route, which he said raised costs by 50%. Stiell described it as delivering a global shock wave hitting households hard. The talks face pressure to deliver after slow progress, amid expectations that global heating will reach at least 1.8C this year, beyond the 1.5C Paris goal. Delegates from nearly 200 countries watched a film urging reconnection with the planet as negotiations move toward new renewable and electrification targets.
items.title: UN Climate Chief Warns Fossil Fuel Prices Spread Inflation Like Cancer at Cop31

items.summary: According to a report from the China Enterprise Reform and Development Society, China will spend roughly $940 billion on energy transition capacity and infrastructure this year, keeping it as the world's largest investor. The figure reflects a shift toward grid expansion and support infrastructure amid growing low-carbon generation. State Grid Corporation of China expects up to $574 billion in fixed-asset spending through 2030. Bloomberg reported that coal fell below half of electricity output for the first time, though this may be seasonal. Analysts note overcapacity, cutthroat competition and bankruptcies remain unresolved challenges behind the impressive numbers.
items.title: China Leads Global Energy Transition Spending in 2026

items.summary: Vanderbilt University says it is responding to a cyberattack claimed by the BYOD ransomware gang, which alleges encryption of university databases and theft of student, employee, and research data. The incident was confirmed Monday, with warnings that devices, systems, and cloud services may be affected. Students, faculty, and staff were told to shut down university devices and disconnect from Wi-Fi. Vanderbilt has not disclosed the attack's nature or confirmed whether any data was stolen.
items.title: Vanderbilt University Responds to BYOD Ransomware Attack

items.summary: On Monday, US President Donald Trump told reporters at the White House that further military action against Iran did not appear necessary at this stage, though Washington remained prepared to act if circumstances changed. He said Israel and the wider Middle East were protected from Iranian threats while keeping the status quo.
items.title: Trump Says Military Action Against Iran Not Necessary Now

items.summary: In Rau, Madhya Pradesh, a 40-year-old restaurant owner allegedly stabbed his wife in the neck before hanging himself at their rented house in Sai Vihar Colony during Diwali. Police said a dispute over her suspected affair with a man named Faizan may have triggered it. Their two children survived; Pawan's son claimed his mother wanted them to leave.
items.title: Restaurant Owner Kills Wife Then Commits Suicide in Indore on Diwali

items.summary: Apple paid US$3.25 billion in income taxes to Singapore for its FY2026, the figure disclosed in its annual report covering the year ended Sept 26. The payment reflected about 9.4% of Apple's worldwide cash tax payments and benefited from lower local rates; incentives cut its expense by US$5.49 billion versus a 21% US benchmark, though a US$2.51 billion top-up tax under Singapore's global minimum rate partly offset the savings, leaving an estimated net reduction of about US$2.67 billion. Apple did not disclose its exact effective Singapore rate, and the reports do not establish whether payments rose or fell.
items.title: Apple Pays Record Singapore Income Tax Amid Global Minimum Rules

items.summary: OpenAI will not face criminal penalties over its June access to Services Australia data, but Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced proposed changes to Australia's criminal law targeting future breaches by artificial intelligence companies. A rapid review produced 18 recommendations that the government has accepted and begun implementing, including mandatory AI safety reporting and a new regulator. The home affairs minister said laws must keep pace with technology.
items.title: Australia moves to regulate AI after OpenAI breach

items.summary: Donald Trump defended Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who faces an impeachment resolution from Republican senator Thomas Massie, calling him a leader who 'won two wars.' He also said he was amazed by claims that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy and stated the FBI is now investigating.
items.title: Trump Defends Hegseth and Jensen Huang Over Spy Allegations

items.summary: Anthropic can begin formally marketing its long-awaited initial public offering as early as Tuesday, allowing it to argue that now is a suitable time to go public despite last week's decline in artificial intelligence-related stocks. The Cboe Volatility Index rose above 25 during the past week, entering a range where companies typically delay listings, according to Matt Kennedy of Renaissance Capital.
items.title: Anthropic May Begin Marketing IPO as AI Stocks Swoon

items.summary: On Nov 9, Anthropic sent details of its blockbuster IPO filing to bankers and later retracted them, according to emails seen by Reuters. The company first shared a copy showing it aimed to sell about 867 million shares priced at $70 to $80 per share, then emailed that the pricing details were inaccurate and would update the filing.
items.title: Anthropic Sends and Retracts IPO Filing Details in Emails Seen by Reuters

items.summary: Jensen Huang, boss of Nvidia, admitted an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed that US officials say acted as an agent for Beijing's Ministry of State Security. American authorities have investigated the company and Ms Huang for years over alleged efforts to move high-grade Nvidia chips into China, which prompted strict export controls. The New York Times reported intelligence about their relationship was shown to President Trump last year with no direct action taken. Trump said the FBI is also investigating and that Mr Huang claimed ignorance of any spying. Beijing denies the allegations as smears; Global Times called it a political witch hunt lacking hard evidence, saying the affair posed no technical risk. Nvidia says no secrets were leaked but will bring in outside counsel.
items.title: Nvidia Chief Investigated Over Alleged Spy Affair

items.summary: President Donald Trump said on Monday that the FBI is investigating Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang's relationship with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of being a spy for Beijing. Trump told reporters he knew about the investigation and believed Huang would be in good shape, adding that Huang had spoken to him and did not know the woman was a spy. The statement intensifies questions over national security concerns surrounding Huang's ties to the administration, according to reporting on the controversy. Trump attributed all claims directly; no figures were provided by the item.
items.title: Trump Says FBI Investigating Jensen Huang's Ties to Alleged Chinese Spy

items.summary: Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani characterised digital life and services as a multi-wave business rather than one built on a single component. He made the remark in September 2016, shortly after launching Reliance Jio's commercial operations at RIL's annual general meeting. The framing suggests connectivity is only an entry point to acquire users before later technology layers follow.
items.title: Mukesh Ambani Frames Digital Business as Multi-Wave Enterprise

items.summary: A New York Times report alleges that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang maintained a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of passing information to the Chinese government. Following the disclosure, Nvidia launched an internal probe and its shares fell to a seven-month low on Monday. Senator Chris Coons called for investigation into whether national security was compromised.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Faces Foreign Intelligence Scrutiny Over Trump Ties

items.summary: Qantas announced on Nov 10 it would cut 850 jobs across finance, procurement, human resources and marketing as part of a multi-year partnership with Accenture. The airline said some roles would shift to teams mostly based in India. CEO Vanessa Hudson noted the cuts affect around 3% of its Australian workforce of 28,000, with the first round by mid-2027.
items.title: Qantas Cuts 850 Jobs in Accenture Offshoring Deal

items.summary: US President Donald Trump said Monday that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang should not worry about an FBI investigation into a woman alleged to be a Chinese government agent. Speaking at a White House briefing, Trump stated he believes Huang will be in good shape and described him as honorable. The affair has raised concerns about whether China accessed Nvidia's AI chips. Nvidia launched its own independent investigation Sunday after reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Shares fell roughly 5 per cent Monday. China denied any involvement, calling the allegations unsubstantiated smears.
items.title: Trump Defends Nvidia Chief Amid Spy Allegations and FBI Inquiry

items.summary: The Nvidia board, including director Aarti Shah, has launched an independent investigation into whether its 63-year-old chief executive was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The allegations remain unproven and are described as explosive but not yet established. Beijing denied the claims, calling them "nothing but smears against China." US intelligence officials reportedly concluded that Alice Huang had been recruited to cultivate a relationship with Jensen Huang to obtain information about Nvidia's advanced processors. The matter coincides with an upcoming Trump-Xi meeting at APEC in Shenzhen on November 18-19 and closed-door briefings requested by House committees. Nvidia's board stated it had "no reason to believe" national security or company secrets were compromised while examining all available information.
items.title: Nvidia Board Launches Probe Into Alleged Chinese Espionage Ties

items.summary: In a medium-confidence analysis, the authors argue that frontier AI companies should begin pacing development soon and propose verified compute allocation disclosures (VCAD) as its foundational step. VCAD would require regular reports on how compute is used—such as distinguishing AI R&D from safety R&D or external inference—and verification by third-party auditors, ideally with government support. The authors claim VCAD underpins nearly all pacing proposals less extreme than shutting off GPUs, because attacks typically involve doing prohibited work on unmonitored compute. They also argue that slowing software progress is more effective than only delaying training runs, warning of a 'software overhang' risk. The post concludes that developing and battle-testing the process should be treated as urgent given how quickly capable AIs are advancing.
items.title: AI Safety Researchers Pitch Verified Compute Disclosure as Pacing Foundation

items.summary: A truck driver living near a proposed $5 billion Amazon data center in Butler County, Ohio, has led community efforts to block the project. Barry Blankenship of St. Clair Township organized opposition through the Woodsdale and Trenton Environmental Resistance group, citing concerns about water use, noise and pollution from backup generators. The St. Clair Township Zoning Commission passed a resolution calling for a complete ban on data centers, which was sent to the Butler County Rural Zoning Commission hearing scheduled for 10 November at 3:00 p. m. , with final authority resting with township trustees. In nearby Trenton, voters approved banning data centers larger than 25 megawatts by 80 percent in March 2026 elections. The opposition reflects broader resistance across Ohio, where at least 14 municipalities and townships adopted restrictions during November 2026 elections. Higher electricity bills and power demands for artificial intelligence infrastructure became major concerns among voters supporting these restrictions.
items.title: Ohio Truck Driver Leads Campaign Against Amazon Data Center

items.summary: The arrest of a former OpenAI engineer for planting a listening device at Nvidia's San Francisco headquarters, alongside the conviction and later partial acquittal of Google engineer Linwei Ding, suggests traditional espionage remains relevant despite advances in artificial intelligence. US agencies believed Alice Huang worked for Beijing while cultivating a relationship with Jensen Huang to gather information on chip export restrictions; these allegations remain unverified publicly, as Singapore declined to investigate her. Nvidia's board announced an independent inquiry but stated it has no reason to believe its secrets were compromised.
items.title: Nvidia Spy Scandal Revives Human Espionage in AI Race

items.summary: The Senate advanced bipartisan legislation on Monday, the first major action since last week’s election that repudiated Donald Trump. The bill would speed up permitting for datacenters, pipelines and clean energy projects while rolling back environmental protections like Nepa. Climate advocates are divided: Earthjustice, the Sierra Club and the ACLU oppose it over weakened laws; Indigenous groups warn of tribal consultation erosion. Proponents argue cheap renewables will win in a competitive market. Models conflict on emissions outcomes, with Rhodium Group projecting declines but Purdue’s Kevin Kircher forecasting increases pending peer review.
items.title: Senate Advances Infrastructure Permitting Bill Amid Fossil Fuel and Tribal Concerns

items.summary: A Republican congressman plans to force a House of Representatives vote this week to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, alleging he violated the US Constitution by engaging in hostilities in Iran for more than 90 days without congressional authorisation. Representative Thomas Massie introduced his articles Monday afternoon, starting a 48-hour clock before lawmakers could act. The effort is likely to fail while Republicans hold Congress until January, but Massie frames it as pressure on President Trump to replace Hegseth ahead of Democratic control next year. Hegseth dismissed the move as a sham and called Massie disgruntled and defeated; Trump said he would stick by him.
items.title: Republican congressman pushes impeachment vote on Hegseth

items.summary: European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on Monday she saw little sign of Russian goodwill toward negotiating an end to the war in Ukraine. Speaking at a Group of Seven ministerial meeting, she added that Moscow had signed up to numerous agreements underpinning European security but failed to respect them. When asked directly, Kallas said: “So far they have just been pretending that they negotiate because we haven’t seen any goodwill from the Russian side.” Her remarks came ahead of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi between Ukraine, Russia and the United States.
items.title: EU Foreign Policy Chief Accuses Russia of Pretending to Negotiate While Bombing Civilians

items.summary: Brent crude fell 24 cents, or 0.23%, to $92.33 a barrel by 0102 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) futures dropped 35 cents, or 0.40%, to $86.50 a barrel. Trump said he plans to hold off on new military strikes against Iran after appeals from regional countries including Qatar's prime minister, though he intends to keep a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian security council chief Mohsen Rezaei called for talks to end and urged surrender to seven conditions.
items.title: Trump downplays Iran strikes as oil prices dip

items.summary: A near-fifth drop in crude oil prices helped India's rupee climb among Asia's best-performing currencies through the first two quarters of FY27, gaining 0.97% per Bloomberg data, while the won rose over 11% and Indonesia's rupiah fell 6.24%. Foreign investors bought ₹38,971 crore in equities last week as RBI reportedly intervened to cap gains; its forward book showed a $239 billion net short dollar position as of September 2026. Analysts expect the central bank to rebuild reserves rather than let the rupee strengthen sharply, with Kotak Securities' Anindya Banerjee forecasting it toward 92.50-92.75 near term.
items.title: Rupee Rises as Oil Prices Fall and RBI Eyes Dollar Reserves

items.summary: US President Donald Trump said on Monday that the war with Iran is 'effectively over' militarily, while vowing to keep isolating Tehran economically through a naval blockade and Operation Iron Gate. Quoting him, CBS News reported he hoped for a deal but added nothing would happen without serious consequences. His remarks eased oil-market fears: Brent crude fell more than $7 a barrel to its lowest level since late August, ending the session 5.85% lower at $92.57, while WTI settled at $86.85, down 4.38%. Trump has reportedly deferred an attack after talking with Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani. It remains unclear whether a deal or fresh strikes will follow.
items.title: Trump Calls Iran War Militarily Over as Oil Slumps

items.summary: A Coober Pedy woman has been charged with domestic violence offences against her child, including an allegation of choking that can attract a maximum sentence of seven years. She was remanded in custody and is due to return to court later this month.
items.title: Coober Pedy woman remanded in custody over child choking charge

items.summary: Republican Congressman Thomas Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday, accusing him of waging an unauthorized war in Iran and abusing Pentagon powers. President Trump defended Hegseth, calling his work a success while dismissing Massie as a loser. House Speaker Mike Johnson has blocked prior attempts to vote.
items.title: Massie moves to impeach Hegseth over Iran war as Trump backs him

items.summary: Political discussions in Maharashtra have intensified over a possible merger between the two Nationalist Congress Party factions, with state president Sunil Tatkare confirming that Ajit Pawar had set a framework before 12 February. Shiv Sena leader Sanjay Shirsat said talks are in final stages, but the Sharad Pawar faction refuted these claims through MLA Rohit Pawar, who called it political speculation.
items.title: Maharashtra NCP Factions Explore Possible Merger Amid Political Talks

items.summary: The Department of Science and Technology revised its flagship INSPIRE-Scholarship for Higher Education (SHE) guidelines on November 7, announcing the 2025 batch after a delay of more than a year. Under the changes, students who fail or miss an examination can no longer retain their scholarships; those scoring below 60% in the first year lose eligibility entirely. The ₹20,000 annual mentorship grant is now limited to third and fourth years, reducing maximum support over five years from ₹4 lakh to ₹3.4 lakh. Allocation quotas are tied to Class 12 examinees rather than applications received. Experts warn the rules could reduce awards and leave some board quotas unfilled. DST did not respond to queries for comment.HT reported on July 15 that no notification was issued in 2025, leaving aspirants uncertain about the scheme’s future.
items.title: DST Tightens INSPIRE-SHE Rules, Cuts Mentorship Grant

items.summary: The Telangana Women's Commission questioned five Hyderabad fertility centres over allegations of collecting eggs from poor women for money and using them in illegal IVFs. Chairman Nerella Sarada summoned representatives after a suo motu case on November 7, following arrests linked to the racket. Officials expect to decide further action after reviewing responses.
items.title: Telangana Women's Commission Questions Fertility Centres Over Illegal IVF Allegations

items.summary: President Donald Trump said Monday his administration would not offer amnesty to undocumented immigrants and that its deportation policy remained unchanged. He told reporters at the White House they would focus on removing those convicted of serious crimes like murder and drug trafficking, calling them 'the worst of the worst.' Trump acknowledged some undocumented immigrants have become productive workers with good jobs and may pay taxes.
items.title: Trump Rejects Immigration Amnesty, Vows Unchanged Deportation Policy

items.summary: Rep. Thomas Massie introduced an impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, focusing mainly on the war in Iran but also citing Hegseth's actions in Yemen and Venezuela. A House vote could arrive by mid-week, though next steps are uncertain. Speaker Mike Johnson urged caution amid ongoing hostilities, while most Democrats favor ousting Hegseth. Trump defended him as having won two wars. Hegseth dismissed the effort as politically motivated noise and announced a rare news conference on Tuesday. The push follows Republican midterm losses tied to anger over the Iran war.
items.title: Republican Congressman Launches Impeachment Bid Against Defense Secretary Hegseth

items.summary: The article, titled 'Overheard In Bhopal,' reports on several tensions within Madhya Pradesh's bureaucracy as relayed by unnamed sources. It describes embittered relations between a minister and an IAS officer that reportedly began after disagreements over deals involving sweeteners, with the minister favouring his son. Separately, state head 'Bade Sahib' is said to be angry at an officer during departmental meetings, opposing his transfer despite chaos in the office. The piece also covers other matters: a glorified IPS officer's transfer that angered senior officers; possible reshuffle moves affecting a principal secretary whose name was removed from the list; and a retired woman IAS officer ('Madam') who worked six years before retirement amid claims she holds sensitive information, though others say she never harmed anyone. A sixth item notes another senior officer may face court cases for working without government orders.
items.title: Bureaucratic Feuds and Office Politics in Bhopal Administration

items.summary: Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan and his wife Anna Konidala announced they have decided to end their marriage by mutual consent, prioritising their children's happiness. In a statement issued by the Deputy Chief Minister's office, the couple said the decision was taken with mutual understanding after spending much of their lives together. They described themselves as remaining good friends and devoted parents, asked well-wishers for privacy during this personal transition, and thanked those who supported them throughout their journey. The article notes Pawan Kalyan previously married Nandini in 1997 and Renu Desai in 2009 before marrying Anna in 2013.
items.title: Pawan Kalyan and Anna Konidala Announce Mutual Divorce

items.summary: Roshan Suvarna has sought bail in the Mumbai local train murder case of Mayank Lohar. He denies stabbing the 22-year-old victim and says an unidentified man attacked both him and Lohar before escaping when a chain was pulled between Goregaon and Malad. The victim's family, through advocate Prince Upadhyay, opposes his release as contradictory.
items.title: Mumbai train accused seeks bail, claims he saved victim and real attacker escaped

items.summary: China's trade surplus reached US$1.04 trillion in the first 10 months of 2026, surpassing US$1 trillion for a second consecutive year and hitting the milestone a month earlier than in 2025, customs data showed on Nov 10. Exports rose 35.2% in October from a year earlier, ahead of economists' forecast, while imports grew 41.6%. The gains reflect strong overseas demand for high-tech products as global AI infrastructure investment accelerates, but analysts warn the reliance could deepen domestic imbalances and fuel trade friction with partners including the EU.
items.title: China's trade surplus tops US$1 trillion as AI-driven exports surge, raising EU tensions

items.summary: According to a Focus Taiwan report, Taiwan's semiconductor supply chain sources expect global artificial intelligence demand to remain strong despite the controversy surrounding Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang. While one source noted the dispute could affect the industry over the next six months, others stressed that decades of close supplier relationships and continued investment from cloud providers would sustain long-term growth in Taiwan's chip sector even if leadership changed at Nvidia.
items.title: Taiwan Chipmakers See Limited Long-Term Impact From Jensen Huang Controversy on AI Demand

items.summary: The Chinese foreign ministry on Monday rejected reports alleging that the woman involved in an extramarital affair with Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang was working for Chinese intelligence. Spokesperson Guo Jiakun called the claim unsubstantiated and described it as nothing but smears against China, according to a regular press briefing.
items.title: China's Foreign Ministry Rejects 'Chinese Spy' Claims Over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

items.summary: Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan and his wife, Anna Konidala, announced on Monday (November 10) that they were parting ways after 13 years of marriage. The separation ends Kalyan's third marriage; he was previously married to Nandini and Renu Desai. A statement from the Deputy Chief Minister's office said the decision came with mutual understanding and respect, while the couple said they will remain good friends and devoted parents. Konidala is originally from Russia and studied at the National University of Singapore in 2024; the pair wed on September 30, 2013. The statement was issued through Jana Sena's WhatsApp group, per news agency ANI.
items.title: Who is Anna Konidala of Russia? What Pawan Kalyan shared on WhatsApp group on parting ways

items.summary: Jensen Huang, Nvidia's chief executive, fell from eighth to tenth place on the Forbes real-time billionaires ranking after his net worth dropped $7.4 billion within about half an hour of Monday trading. The fall followed a sharp decline in Nvidia shares amid an investigation into his relationship with Alice Huang, whom US intelligence agencies suspect of gathering information for Beijing. His fortune slid from $162.2 billion to $154.7 billion as shares fell more than 7 per cent at the open and later about 5.5 per cent by early afternoon. Nvidia's board appointed independent directors to review available information, stating it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised. The probe follows a New York Times report citing an administration memo. Huang has apologised to staff and defended himself as honourable; the company is set to report quarterly earnings next Tuesday.
items.title: Nvidia Chief Slips in Forbes Rich List After Spy Probe

items.summary: Wiz, Google's newly acquired cybersecurity unit, reportedly arranged a surprise private Katy Perry concert for employees on a five-day Thailand retreat in Khao Lak. The appearance drew online criticism over celebrities accepting lucrative private bookings while taking public social stances, per Calcalist and Ynet reports. A reported $3 million to $4 million cost covered production, not just her fee.
items.title: Katy Perry's Private Wiz Concert Draws Online Backlash

items.summary: Three workers were killed during water tank maintenance work on Tuesday at Tata Electronics' facility in Hosur, Tamil Nadu. State minister Virudhai Magal Keerthana expressed grief and said she had spoken to the district administration about supporting affected families. She added that an investigation would be conducted and measures taken to prevent such tragedies from recurring.
items.title: Three Workers Killed in Water Tank Maintenance at Tata Electronics Facility in Tamil Nadu

items.summary: President Donald Trump said Monday that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang should not worry about an FBI investigation into his relationship with a woman alleged to be a Chinese government agent, telling reporters at the White House he believes Huang “will be in good shape.” The disclosure has raised concerns about whether China accessed Nvidia chips powering artificial intelligence. Beijing denied any spying effort on Monday, calling it unsubstantiated and a smear campaign. Nvidia launched an independent investigation Sunday; shares fell roughly 5 per cent pre-market Monday.
items.title: Trump Defends Nvidia Chief Amid Spy Probe

items.summary: China's trade surplus reached US$1.04 trillion in the first 10 months, customs data showed Tuesday (Nov 10), as October exports rose 35.2 per cent year-on-year. A global push to build AI infrastructure buoyed high-tech sales and offset weak domestic demand, a dynamic that could sharpen trade tensions with partners including the European Union. Macquarie analysts expect export growth to continue into early 2027.
items.title: China's Trade Surplus Crosses US$1 Trillion on AI-Driven Exports

items.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce announced Monday that it will continue suspending export control measures on 16 US entities for two months, starting Tuesday. A spokesperson said the decision implements consensus from the eighth round of China-US economic and trade consultations held in April 2025. Export operators must apply to the ministry before shipping dual-use items to these entities.
items.title: China Extends Export Control Suspension on US Entities for Two Months

items.summary: China's trade surplus exceeded $1 trillion in a second consecutive year, official data released Tuesday showed. October exports rose 35.2 per cent from a year earlier, the customs agency said, while imports climbed 41.6 per cent. Between January and October the surplus reached $1.04 trillion, down from September's $133.5bn to $105.3bn as imports accelerated. Economists warn overcapacity and trade curbs pose risks; officials say Beijing seeks more balanced global trade rather than a larger surplus.
items.title: China's Trade Surplus Tops $1 Trillion for Second Straight Year

items.summary: Richard Allen, chief executive of a New Zealand dairy company, says the ability to innovate quickly is something his company has learned in China. He adds that this experience holds value beyond its own market, including Southeast Asia. A site notice states that browsing continues under revised privacy and cookie terms.
items.title: NZ Dairy CEO Sees Fast Food Innovation in China

items.summary: CGTN's program "Making It Together — China's Guangdong Industrial Clusters and APEC" examines Shantou, a city in China's Guangdong Province. The piece notes that one out of every three plastic toys worldwide comes from this region, framing the city as a global toy hub whose influence extends across Asia-Pacific markets through growing trade connections.
items.title: Shantou Emerges as Asia-Pacific Toy Hub Through Global Trade Links

items.summary: The Financial Times reported that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive alleged to have been recruited by Chinese intelligence. Huang admitted the relationship and apologized in a Sunday memo while Nvidia investigates independently.
items.title: Nvidia CEO's Alleged Affair With Chinese Spy Under Scrutiny

items.summary: Anthropic is spending $3.4 billion on natural gas turbines, marking a shift from its usual preference for renting computing power to buying physical infrastructure. The purchase involves Caterpillar generators that OnePWR had originally ordered and can produce up to 1.7 gigawatts of electricity. Anthropic disclosed in May it pays xAI $1.25 billion monthly through 2029, but growing demand has made the turbine market uncertain, with backlogs extending into the early 2030s.
items.title: Anthropic Buys $3.4 Billion in Natural Gas Turbines

items.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav pledged to transform Ayodhya into the “global capital of Sanatan pilgrimage”, promising transparent temple administration, world-class infrastructure and steps to revive the local economy ahead of his proposed visit on December 12. He said pilgrims had declined after what he called the theft of the Ram Temple and vowed action against alleged land and circle-rate scams. His post came amid an exchange with Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath, who demanded that those responsible for firing on devotees apologise before visiting, per PTI.
items.title: Akhilesh Yadav vows Ayodhya as global pilgrimage capital

items.summary: Using Medicare Part D data, the Treatment Episode Data Set, and a difference-in-differences design, researchers find naloxone coprescription laws increased naloxone prescribing by 275%, with effects twice as large where prescriptions were required. No rise in opioid or benzodiazepine prescribing was found.
items.title: Naloxone Coprescription Laws Boost Prescribing and Treatment Engagement in the U.S.

items.summary: A field experiment randomized invitation framing in a leading stem-cell registry and found that engagement-initiative participation sorts donors by reliability: participants were unavailable in 12% of cases versus 30% for non-participants. Although the framings reduced initiative participation, intention-to-treat analyses showed no average effect on confirmatory typing availability; prioritizing participants could raise one-year survivors by up to 7.5%. Authors note gains may be larger at registries with lower availability.
items.title: Stem-Cell Registry Test Finds Opting In Signals Reliability

items.summary: Tan Soon Hock raises in a Straits Times forum whether people who help disqualified drivers access deregistered vehicles should face charges. The driver involved in the fatal Tampines crash that killed two was handed nine charges, including using a deregistered vehicle despite being banned until 2032. Land Transport Authority officials investigated 122 such cases in the first five months of 2026.
items.title: Forum Questions Measures Against Deregistered Cars Returning to Roads

items.summary: Donald Trump told reporters at a White House briefing that renewed US strikes on Iran were 'highly unlikely,' while saying the country remained 'locked and loaded' if circumstances changed. He described negotiations as showing positive momentum after hosting Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdul Rahman Al Thani, who called their talks excellent. Iranian officials have repeatedly doubted Trump's earlier claims about resolving the conflict.
items.title: Trump says renewed US attacks on Iran are highly unlikely

items.summary: One Nation Victoria disendorsed candidate Franco Guardiani after his deleted X post called Adolf Hitler the “GOAT” and claimed importing Islam legalised pedophilia. The party learned of the posts Tuesday morning, confirmed them with an official, and removed him from its website. Leader Warren Pickering said Jewish Australians face unprecedented persecution and that anyone holding such views has no place in One Nation.
items.title: One Nation Victoria Disendorsed Candidate Over Hitler GOAT Post

items.summary: Qantas announced Tuesday it will cut 850 jobs, roughly 3 per cent of its Australian workforce of 28,000. Chief executive Vanessa Hudson said the reductions reflect a global shift toward technology and artificial intelligence, with roles moving to India through partner Accenture over coming years, first by mid-2027. The airline also flagged Australia's largest fleet renewal in history, adding 17 aircraft last year and expecting up to 31 more next year, retiring the A380 from 2028.
items.title: Qantas Trims Workforce and Aims for AI-Driven Transformation Amid Fleet Renewal

items.summary: The Bank of Japan's summary of its Oct. 29-30 policy meeting indicated that many board members see a near-term interest rate hike as necessary, pointing to a good chance of action in December. Following sustained price gains, the central bank has accelerated its pace of hikes. One of nine board members said the bank should decide on the next hike when possible without becoming overly cautious.
items.title: Bank of Japan Signals Likely December Rate Hike

items.summary: Two former NSW police officers jailed for assaulting Jodi Knott during her psychosis have had their maximum prison terms reduced after an appeal, the ABC reports. Ms Knott's family are 'gutted'. The Court of Criminal Appeal found aggravating cruelty was double-counted but upheld that pepper-spray misuse and brutality were at the top range; both men may be released as early as next year. Justice Hament Dhanji called it a 'shocking lack of humanity.' Ms Knott died of cancer 18 months after the 2023 attack, and in July NSW introduced a health-led mental-health response model moving away from police interventions.
items.title: Family outraged as police assaulters' sentences cut

items.summary: The European Union announced €50 million for a maritime security hub to be developed in Constanța and Varna, with completion on a clear timeline. President Ursula von der Leyen said the EU stands "in full solidarity" with Romania and can offer satellite imagery from Copernicus. The announcement follows Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev accusing Romania of indirect responsibility for attacks on commercial ships without evidence. According to Euronews, the hub could become operational in the first half of next year; Florentina Lazar said its objectives include protecting infrastructure, sharing information and supporting trade.
items.title: EU Funds Black Sea Maritime Security Hub in Romania and Bulgaria

items.summary: Crude oil prices fell sharply on Tuesday after US President Donald Trump said he believes the war in Iran is effectively over. Brent crude dropped 81 cents, or 0.88%, to below $92 a barrel, while WTI slipped 79 cents, or 0.91%, to $86 a barrel. Brent had already fallen 5.85% in the previous session to its lowest since August 31. Trump said Iran is militarily decapitated but he still wants a long-term solution to defang its nuclear programme. Goldman Sachs raised oil forecasts, warning Brent could reach $140 per barrel by 2027 if Gulf production stays low; it lifted December Brent to $105 from $90 and WTI to $94 from $81. JPMorgan said the conflict remains hard to predict.
items.title: Oil Falls Below $92 as Trump Says Iran War Is Over

items.summary: M John Harrison has won the 2026 Booker Prize for The End of Everything, receiving £50,000 and a trophy. At 81, he becomes the oldest author to win in the prize's history, with a career spanning 60 years; this was also his first nomination. Jury chair Mary Beard called it a book that raises 'a wry smile' yet leaves optimism.
items.title: Oldest Booker Winner Yet Takes Prize for Dystopian Novel

items.summary: As COP31 opens in Antalya, Turkey, the presidency proposes raising electricity’s share of global final energy use to 35% by 2035. Authors Pallavi Das and Vaibhav Chaturvedi argue the slogan sounds appealing but raise whether it matters, is achievable, and how a single number could be shared fairly. They note cost-effective electrification reaches only about 33%, with fuel-importing countries potentially saving more than $400 billion by 2035 versus 2025. Starting points differ widely: developed nations flatlined near 21%-25% since 2010, while India rose from 14% to 19%. Their analysis projects India reaching roughly 27%, so a uniform target ignores differentiated pathways and per-capita use.
items.title: COP31's '35 by 35' electrification goal faces fairness and realism questions

items.summary: A Utah judge scheduled Tyler Robinson's trial, set to begin June 21, 2028, with jury selection starting that day and proceedings lasting up to 105 days. The decision followed the defence proposing a 2029 start while prosecutors argued readiness by October 2027. Erika Kirk's lawyer Jeffrey Neiman called the timeline not very speedy, and the family described it as a delay. Robinson pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder in connection with the September 10, 2025 shooting of Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University and could face the death penalty if convicted.
items.title: Utah Judge Sets Trial Date for Charlie Kirk's Killer Three Years Later

items.summary: A Supreme Court bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana directed the governments of Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan to submit a detailed action plan within two weeks covering vehicular movement, emission standards and measures against polluting vehicles. The matter will next be heard on November 23 amid worsening air quality in the region.
items.title: Supreme Court Orders Pollution Action Plan From Delhi-NCR Governments

items.summary: A post-Diwali 'Hingot War' clash in Gautampura, Madhya Pradesh, left 20 people injured on Monday evening, a health department official said. Block Medical Officer Dr Vibha Nagar told PTI that six were admitted to a primary health centre while 14 with minor burns received first aid and went home. The annual Turra versus Kalangi battle involves hurling gunpowder-filled fruit shells; spectators are protected by nets and drones, though injuries recur each year.
items.title: Injuries in Indore Hingot War ritual

items.summary: British author M. John Harrison won the 2026 Booker Prize for his dystopian novel 'The End of Everything,' becoming the oldest winner in the award's history at age 81. He received £50,000 ($67,232) at a ceremony in London where last year's winner David Szalay presented it. Historian Mary Beard chaired the panel that unanimously selected the book after reviewing 163 submissions.
items.title: Eighty-One-Year-Old Author Becomes Oldest Booker Prize Winner

items.summary: The Hindustan Times morning brief of November 10, 2025 roundups several headlines. United States President Donald Trump said on Monday that US military action in Iran is 'effectively over'. British author M John Harrison won the 2026 Booker Prize for his novel The End of Everything at age 81, becoming the oldest winner and the first science fiction writer to do so.
items.title: Hindustan Times morning brief covers Iran war claim and Booker Prize win

items.summary: Chief Minister DK Shivakumar announced on November 1 that the Congress government would seek official recognition for Karnataka's traditional red-and-yellow Kannada flag, allowing it to be hoisted alongside the national flag at government offices and events. The move comes amid upcoming May 2028 assembly elections and is seen as a counter-narrative to BJP nationalism. While activists welcome the gesture, constitutional questions about state flags remain unresolved. Veteran activist Ra Nam Chandrashekar called it significant for Karnataka's identity within India's federal structure.
